title: Resource mapping & lifecycle: API playbook (routing-first)
content:
Purpose:
A compact playbook that ties the control-plane resource model (resources, environments, regions, clusters) to the CRUD APIs and routing policies. This is routing-first: design decisions prioritize deterministic routing behavior and operational simplicity for multi-region deployments.

Quick summary:
- Single canonical resource record per logical resource (ResourceRecord).
- Environment scope (dev/stage/prod) is orthogonal to region binding. Resources can be global, cross-region, or region-bound.
- Routing decisions are derived from a small set of attributes: resource type, tenancy, region affinity, availability tier, and active version.
- CRUD semantics are strongly idempotent with explicit eventual-consistency markers for cross-region propagation.

Core entities (brief):
- ResourceRecord: id, type, owner_id, environment, desired_region (optional), region_bindings (list), active_version, creation_ts, update_ts, annotations.
- Environment: logical grouping (dev|staging|prod|sandbox) with policy flags (allow_cross_region, allow_public_ingress).
- Region: physical location (us-west1, eu-central1, ap-southeast1), with health and capacity metadata.
- Cluster: compute grouping inside a region (cluster-id, zone, GPUs, labels).
- RoutePolicy: declarative rule used by the control plane to map incoming requests to ResourceRecords / model variants.

Canonical ID and naming conventions:
- resource_id: <org>-<env>-<type>-<shortname>-<uuid4>
  - Example: redwood-prod-model-embedder-7f3c2a4e
- Avoid semantic IDs that encode region or cluster. Use attributes instead (desired_region, region_bindings).
- Shortname should be human-readable; UUID ensures uniqueness across tenants.

CRUD contract highlights:
- Create (POST /v1/resources)
  - Accepts desired_region (optional), environment, owner_id, spec blob, tenancy (shared|dedicated).
  - Returns 202 + resource_id when async provisioning starts.
- Read (GET /v1/resources/{id})
  - Always returns the canonical ResourceRecord. Include per-region propagation_status map (enum: pending|synced|failed).
- Update (PATCH /v1/resources/{id})
  - Partial updates allowed. Mutating region_bindings or tenancy triggers a "reconcile" workflow.
  - Use optimistic concurrency via update_ts or version token header.
- Delete (DELETE /v1/resources/{id})
  - Soft-delete semantics: mark tombstone + start deprovisioning in bound regions. DELETE returns 202 with deprovision_job_id.

Idempotency and concurrency model:
- All mutating endpoints accept Idempotency-Key header. Operations are idempotent within a 24h window.
- For cross-region bound resources, updates are applied to the canonical record first, then fan-out to region controllers. Each region returns a per-region status to the central record.
- Conflict resolution: last-writer-wins at canonical layer, but specific fields (e.g., active_version) support compare-and-set via precondition header.

Routing policy model (how traffic is resolved):
- Inputs used by router:
  - request.region_hint (from SDK or geo-IP)
  - resource.environment
  - route policy overrides (customer or internal)
  - availability tier (gold/silver/best-effort)
  - active_version and compatible_fallbacks
- Routing evaluation order (fast, side-effect-free):
  1) Hard binding: if resource.region_bindings contains request.region => route to that cluster
  2) Soft affinity: prefer desired_region if capacity healthy
  3) Policy overrides: explicit route policies (canary, canary-by-region, blackhole)
  4) Fallbacks: find nearest healthy region with matching tenancy and tier
- Fallbacks respect data residency: if resource.environment disallows cross-region, fail-fast with 409 and a typed error.

Multi-region propagation & consistency guarantees:
- Strong canonical truth: the control-plane central DB is the source of truth. Regions are eventual replicas for routing and runtime config.
- Propagation mechanisms: CDC stream -> regional control-plane caches -> regional agents reconcile local state.
- Each ResourceRecord has propagation_version and per-region last_applied_version.
- SLA expectations: normal propagation expected < 10s within a region pair in same cloud region; cross-cloud may be up to 60s.
- Operators can mark "strict_consistency=true" on a resource to force synchronous fanout (higher latency) during critical migrations.

Operational behaviors and observability needs:
- Expose per-resource: active route counts, average route latency by region, last_reconcile_ts, propagation_status per region.
- Alerting:
  - Region-agent failure > 60s
  - Propagation lag > 120s for prod resources
  - Reconcile failure rate > 1% over 5m window
- Tracing: include resource_id and reconcile_job_id in traces for correlation.

API examples (short):
- POST /v1/resources
  - body: { "shortname":"embedder","type":"model","environment":"prod","desired_region":"eu-central1","tenancy":"shared","spec":{...} }
  - returns: 202, {"resource_id":"redwood-prod-model-embedder-7f3c2a4e","deprovision_job_id":null}
- GET /v1/resources?environment=prod&type=model&region=eu-central1
  - supports filtering by region affinity and tenancy.

Edge cases and chosen tradeoffs:
- Do not auto-failover across regions if a resource explicitly disallows cross-region; this avoids silent policy violations.
- We accept eventual consistency in exchange for low-latency writes to the canonical control plane. For strict windows we provide explicit flags.
- Resource relocation: moving a resource between regions is a multi-step operation (lock canonical record -> provision in target region -> shift active_version -> deprovision source). Expose a helper API /v1/resources/{id}/relocate to orchestrate.

Migration notes (from current proto model):
- Current state: many service-owned records encode region into the id/name. Migration plan: create a compatibility shim that populates desired_region from legacy id, write new canonical records, and flip producers to use canonical resource_id.
- Backwards-compat endpoint: GET /v1/legacy-resources/{legacy-id} -> canonical mapping.

Open questions (for design review):
- How to model per-route soft quotas vs global quotas? (do we attach quota objects to ResourceRecord or keep separate Quota entity?)
- Should we expose a "routing weight" per region at resource level for gradual traffic shifting? (helps staged failover)
- Do we need multi-tenant isolation primitives beyond tenancy field (e.g., resource-affinity groups)?

Next steps / action items:
- Align on canonical ResourceRecord JSON schema (Priya + Diego) -- due 2026-03-08
- Prototype relocate API (Marta) -- POC in feature branch by 2026-03-22
- Add propagation metrics to region-agent (SRE) and wire dashboards (observability backlog)

Notes / references / quick links:
- Confluence: CP entity model v1 (legacy) -> confluence:CP-entity-model-v1
- Jira: PLAT-1347 (routing policy engine), PLAT-1412 (region-agent metrics)
- Slack threads: #platform-routing (see thread pinned message)

Informal thoughts (scratchpad):
- prefer explicit fields to magic strings; less guessing for routing.
- keep API surfaces small: routing outcome should be a deterministic function of canonical record + request hints + policy.
- When in doubt, err on the side of making the canonical record the single place to look during incident response.

-- end of draft --
